title: Elastic top-up lanes: fair-pricing reconciliation and temporary capacity governance
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated often need short windows of extra throughput for seasonal spikes or scheduled events. We already expose 'top-up' bursts via admin surge pools, but current behavior creates confusing invoices and ad-hoc operator interventions. This ticket designs and implements a deterministic, fair proration model and governance controls for temporary capacity lanes ("top-up lanes").

Goals:
- Define a deterministic proration algorithm that maps consumed top-up tokens to billable units with minimal post-hoc adjustments.
- Surface operator controls for emergency top-ups and revoke flows without breaking SLO or billing guarantees.
- Introduce a smoothing window that avoids micro-billing for sub-minute spikes while preserving cost signals.
- Provide clear UI/console and billing artifacts so customers understand why an overage was charged and how it was computed.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term reserved capacity or committed plans.
- Deep changes to existing invoice formats beyond adding an explanatory line item and link to a reconciliation report.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side implementation applies proration rule and emits per-topup ledger entries to billing-stream
Console shows a Top-up usage timeline and single-click download of reconciliation CSV within 48 hours of event
Operator page allows pause/revoke/top-up-expiry extension and captures audit log with reason
Automated tests cover edge cases: overlapping top-ups, partially used allocations, and force-revoke by operator
decisions: Use a time-weighted proration model (billable_units = ceil((allocated_seconds * provisioned_throughput) / billing_unit_seconds)) to avoid micro-charges
Introduce a 5-minute smoothing window during which small spikes (< 10% of baseline throughput and < 30s duration) are not billed as a top-up
Ledger will record both 'provisioned_capacity' and 'consumed_capacity' columns so post-facto refunds can be computed deterministically
Operator revokes will mark top-ups as 'revoked' and trigger a reconciliation pass that may prorate future invoice lines but will not retroactively debit customers for previously invoiced usage

2025-02-21: UX mockups for Console top-up timeline reviewed with PM and Design (feedback: make reconciliation CSV column names explicit)
2025-02-25: integration tests failing for overlapping top-ups — identified race in allocation window; added optimistic allocation lock to allocator service

risks: Race conditions when multiple top-ups overlap for same tenant leading to double-counting without strict ordering
Customer confusion if operator revokes immediately after heavy consumption — requires clear policy and refund path
Edge-case where smoothing window suppresses required capacity leading to degraded p99 latency if autoscaler doesn't react quickly
mitigations: Use per-tenant sequence numbers for top-up operations and idempotent ledger writes
Add 'immediate refund hold' flag that Finance can use during disputes and an automated audit for force-refunds
Tune autoscaler to consider 'provisional allocations' when smoothing suppresses billing signals; add an observability dashboard for suppressed-events vs latency
